# Results — Study 373 (Dispersion-Trade)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The **dispersion trade** —
sell index volatility, buy single-name volatility, said to harvest a "reliably cheap"
index vol — tested on a **transparent realized-vol proxy**. Implied vols / variance swaps
are not free on yfinance, so we build the dispersion from realized vol: rolling 21-day
realized vol of **SPY** (the index) vs. the equal-weight average realized vol of a fixed
**40-name** large-cap basket (the single-name leg). The gap is `avg_single_vol −
index_vol`; the carry book is long single-name variance / short index variance, struck at
a trailing 63-day reference. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — SPY + a fixed 40-name large-cap basket (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-02-02 → 2026-06-18 (**5,378** proxy days; **21.4** years) |
| Realized vol | rolling **21-day** annualised stdev of daily returns (×√252) |
| Dispersion gap | `mean(single-name vol) − index vol`; **PROXY** for the implied-corr dispersion premium |
| Carry book | long single-name variance / short index variance, struck at trailing **63-day** gap |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag on the strike; vega/bid-ask cost = 5e-4 var-pt × 12 re-strikes/yr |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The real trade is an **implied-vol /
> implied-correlation** position (sell index variance swaps, buy single-name variance
> swaps); we only have **realized** vol, so the gap and its carry are a *realized-vol
> proxy* for that object, labelled throughout. A fixed surviving-names basket is the
> *vol-of-the-survivors* — calmer single names, a *narrower* dispersion gap — so the
> survivorship bias runs **against** the believers' free-lunch claim, if anything. The
> verdict does not hinge on the proxy's exact magnitude: it hinges on (1) the gap being a
> near-mechanical identity and (2) the carry failing a robust *t* ≥ 2.

## The gap is reliably positive — but that is an identity, not an edge

Index variance is a correlation-weighted average of single-name variances; under a
one-factor approximation `σ_index ≈ √ρ · avg_single_σ`, so for pairwise correlation ρ < 1
the index vol is **strictly below** the average single-name vol. The realized gap confirms
it almost without exception:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean index vol (SPY, 21d realized) | **15.6%** |
| mean avg single-name vol (basket) | **24.2%** |
| **mean dispersion gap** | **+8.5 vol pts** |
| share of days the gap is **> 0** | **99.6%** |
| implied-by-realized correlation `(σ_idx/avg_σ)²` | **0.41** |

The "index vol is cheap" headline is **true and near-mechanical**: it is subadditivity of
volatility, a no-arbitrage identity. A signal that is positive 99.6% of the time *by
construction* is not a free lunch — it is the cost of the correlation insurance the index
seller is short.

## The carry of the trade — thin, fat-tailed, and not significant

Holding the long-single / short-index variance book (struck at the trailing 63-day gap, so
we earn the dispersion *above what was already priced in*), with a 1-day lag on the strike:

| stat | value |
|---|--:|
| n (daily carry obs) | 5,315 |
| annualised Sharpe | **0.17** |
| win-rate (P[daily carry > 0]) | **44%** |
| naive *t* (mean vs 0) | 0.76 |
| **HAC *t*** (Newey–West, 21 lags) | **0.19** |
| block-sign-flip placebo *p* | **0.43** |

Read it carefully. The carry's **win-rate is only 44%** — you *bleed* most days and are
paid in rare dispersion spikes (daily carry **skew +4.1**). Annualised Sharpe is **0.17**,
and once you correct the *t* for the heavy autocorrelation of overlapping realized-vol
windows, the **HAC *t* is 0.19** — the carry is statistically indistinguishable from zero,
and a block-sign-flip placebo matches it **43%** of the time. There is no robust edge here:
the *gap* is real (an identity), the *carry that monetizes it* is inside the noise.

## Costs barely matter — which is itself the point

| | annualised carry | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| gross | +8.2 var-pts | 0.17 |
| net @ 5e-4 × 12 re-strikes/yr | +7.6 var-pts | **0.15** |

A realistic vega/bid-ask charge shaves only ~0.6 var-pts off the annual carry — costs are
**not** the binding constraint. The binding constraint is that the gross Sharpe is **0.17**
and the stream is **negatively-median, positively-skewed convexity**: you finance a slow
bleed for an occasional payoff that, historically, arrives *with the crash that also blows
up the rest of your book*. The worst carry days cluster in **June 2009** (worst single day
**−15 vol-pts²**), exactly when realized correlation stayed pinned near 1 after the GFC —
the dispersion seller's nightmare.

## Robustness — flat in the vol window

| realized-vol window | gap > 0 share | carry Sharpe | naive *t* | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10-day | 99.2% | 0.14 | 0.64 | **0.18** | 0.422 |
| **21-day** (headline) | 99.6% | 0.17 | 0.76 | **0.19** | 0.425 |
| 42-day | 100.0% | 0.21 | 0.94 | **0.21** | 0.423 |
| 63-day | 100.0% | 0.24 | 1.11 | **0.25** | 0.400 |

Lengthening the window mechanically *smooths* the carry and nudges the naive Sharpe up to
0.24 — but the **HAC *t* never approaches 2** (max 0.25). There is no window at which the
realized-proxy carry clears the bar.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and the mechanical gap fakes nothing

On a deterministic one-factor correlated basket (planted pairwise ρ ≈ 0.35, equal-weight
index), the detector recovers the implied correlation and the carry inference behaves
exactly as it should:

| planted daily carry | gap > 0 share | carry mean | Sharpe | naive *t* | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0000** (no edge) | 100% | +0.00000 | 0.00 | 0.02 | **0.00** | 0.50 |
| **+0.0004** (small edge) | 100% | +0.00040 | 1.91 | 7.54 | **2.10** | 0.019 |
| **+0.0010** (large edge) | 100% | +0.00100 | 4.78 | 18.83 | **5.25** | 0.000 |

With **zero** planted carry the mechanical gap is still positive **100%** of the time, yet
the carry P&L is flat (HAC *t* = **0.00**, placebo *p* = **0.50**): **subadditivity does
not manufacture a tradable carry.** A small planted edge just clears HAC *t* = 2.1; a large
one lights up at 5.25. (Implied-correlation recovery: planted ρ = 0.2/0.4/0.6 → measured
0.19/0.36/0.55.) The control proves the engine is unbiased **and** that the real-tape HAC
*t* of 0.19 is exactly what an *absent* carry edge looks like through this machinery.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The dispersion *gap* is real and reliably positive (99.6% of days,
  +8.5 vol-pts) — but that is the **subadditivity identity**, not an edge, and the *carry*
  that would monetize "cheap index vol" fails the bar decisively: **HAC *t* = 0.19**,
  placebo *p* = 0.43, Sharpe 0.17, win-rate 44%. Real-as-identity, weak-as-edge ⇒ **WEAK**,
  not REAL. (Survivorship in the basket biases the gap *narrower*, against the claim.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Costs barely matter (net Sharpe 0.15); the killer is that the
  realized-proxy carry is a **negative-median, +4.1-skew convexity** stream whose rare
  payoffs cluster in the very crashes (June 2009) that detonate a short-correlation book.
  A Sharpe-0.15 stream you must finance through a slow bleed is **not** a NAV-scale strategy.
- **Free lunch? — BUSTED.** "Index vol is reliably cheap" confuses an **identity**
  (subadditivity makes index vol mechanically lower) with an **edge** (a predictable carry).
  The synthetic control nails it: a basket with **zero** planted carry shows the gap
  positive 100% of the time and a carry of exactly zero. The cheapness is the *premium for
  being short correlation* — priced, not free.
